picks.title: Voxis from CEDAR Audio
picks.excerpt: CEDAR Audio's Voxis is a low-latency voice isolator optimised for live environments, pulling speech and vocals out of troublesome background noise in real time.
picks.rationale: Source separation crosses from offline post into the live console — the latency constraint that kept AI isolation out of realtime work just dropped.

picks.title: Universal and Sony file amended Suno lawsuit after judge gives all clear to add stream ripping claims
picks.excerpt: A judge cleared UMG and Sony to add claims that Suno acquired training data by stream-ripping YouTube; the majors have now filed the amended complaint.
picks.rationale: Freshest legal turn: how training data was obtained — not just what the model outputs — becomes the decisive question for every generative music tool.

picks.title: Free Generative Sequencer For iPad & Mac, Organismi OR-1
picks.excerpt: Organismi Instruments OR-1 is a free generative MIDI sequencer for iPad and Mac that creates "patterns that breathe on their own," evolving material algorithmically rather than from fixed step programming.
picks.rationale: Generative composition arrives as a free everyday sketching tool — a concrete change to how ideas get started, not an AI-industry headline.

picks.title: Dr Dre has words for those who oppose the use of AI in music: "You sound like the person that would have been against the drum machine"
picks.excerpt: Dr Dre says he is actively using AI in production and compares resistance to it with earlier panic over drum machines and synthesizers, drawing sharp pushback from parts of the industry.
picks.rationale: A canonical producer normalising AI in the studio in public — a marker of how fast the craft norm, not just the tooling, is moving.

picks.title: The End of the Definitive Recording
picks.excerpt: An argument that recording is shifting from fixed, definitive versions to adaptive, generative experiences reshaped per listener and context by AI systems.
picks.rationale: Challenges the master recording as a finished design object — what does 'done' mean when playback itself is generative?
